task: Prioritising enterprise IT incidents from report text
method: Fuzzy Q-learning on BERT embeddings
uncertainty: Linguistic vagueness modelled with fuzzy sets
constraint: Fuzzy rule base defines states; no enforcement
env: 10,000 incident reports from one enterprise (2,000 annotated) and a deployment trial
baselines: Static fuzzy rules; BERT classifier; logistic regression
metrics: Priority accuracy; manual overrides; escalation rate; MTTR
result: 82.9% priority accuracy against 78.6% for BERT; overrides 15.2% to 6.2%, escalation rate 11.8% to 9.2% and MTTR down 9.1% in a before-after deployment comparison
limitation: Proprietary data; hand-built rule base; deployment results are before-after, without a control
title: A Hybrid Mathematical Framework for Dynamic Incident Prioritization Using Fuzzy Q-Learning and Text Analytics
venue: Mathematics

task: SOC alert triage learned offline from reconstructed trajectories
method: BC, recurrent BC, GRU/LSTM, CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer
uncertainty: Recurrent context over alert sequences
act: Contain action
esc: Containment left to analysts in the deployment design (not learned)
constraint: Deterministic severity floor in deployment: medium and high alerts cannot be auto-dismissed (design, not evaluated)
env: UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS-2017 flows regrouped into decision episodes
baselines: Memoryless behavioural cloning and six other learners
metrics: MCC, F1, ROC-AUC, per-seed stability
robustness: Chronological future test fold; five seeds; two datasets
result: Recurrent behavioural cloning best (MCC 0.752 and 0.621); CQL, IQL and Decision Transformer degenerated into trivial detectors that F1 and ROC-AUC concealed and MCC revealed
limitation: Trajectories are reconstructed from flow records, not logged analyst decisions
title: A leakage-free benchmark of offline policy learning for SOC alert triage
venue: Machine Learning with Applications

task: Adapting intrusion recovery and response policies
method: Feature-based belief aggregation and rollout
uncertainty: Belief over hidden compromise state; alert distributions measured on a testbed
act: Recovery, decoy, removal and restore controls
constraint: Recovery and service disruption carry costs
env: Physical testbed with emulated attacks (24,386 measurements) and the CAGE-2 benchmark
baselines: Periodic recovery policy; PPO; PPG; DQN; POMCP; C-POMCP; Cardiff
metrics: Cost; time to recovery; recovery frequency; adaptation time
robustness: Non-stationary scenarios on the testbed and CAGE-2
result: On par with the state of the art on CAGE-2; adapted to system change in about 15-19 s against more than 30 min for PPO; PPO variance about ten times higher
limitation: Needs a model or simulator; assumes a static attacker; depends on feature design
title: Adaptive Network Security Policies via Belief Aggregation and Rollout
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security

task: Automated threat response in an IoT network
method: Tabular Q-learning
uncertainty: Not represented
act: Block or counter-attack
env: Simulated IoT network (RL environment not described)
metrics: Learned Q-values; response effectiveness score (not defined)
result: Learned policy blocks mild attacks and counter-attacks severe ones; reported only as a three-state Q-table
limitation: RL result is a Q-table and an undefined score; counter-attacking is reported as a response action
title: An AI-Driven Cybersecurity Framework for IoT: Integrating LSTM-Based Anomaly Detection, Reinforcement Learning, and Post-Quantum Encryption
venue: IEEE Access

task: Proactive threat prediction with RL-controlled mitigation

uncertainty: Latent threat representation

constraint: Mitigation cost in the reward

baselines: Values reported by other studies only
metrics: Containment probability; response latency; several undefined indices
result: Reports containment probability 0.954 and 82 ms response latency
limitation: No baseline in the same environment; several metrics are not defined
title: An Intelligent Proactive Cyber Threat Prediction Model Leveraging Self-Supervised Deep Learning and Reinforcement-Based Control Strategies
venue: 2026 International Conference on Trends in Quantum Computing and Emerging Business Technologies, TQCEBT 2026

task: Enterprise remediation decisions in cloud operations
method: Multi-agent scoring with PPO-tuned weights; IPO constraint solver
uncertainty: Not represented
act: Scale, throttle, restart, isolate, rollback
esc: Hand-off to a human when the safety check fails (rule-triggered)
constraint: Feasible action region plus deterministic execution guard; CMDP cost constraints
env: Google Cluster Trace v3 workloads on a prototype
baselines: Legacy scripts; predictive AIOps; MAS Cloud; AIOpsLab
metrics: MTTR; autonomous resolution rate; governance compliance rate (GCR); cost
result: MTTR 142 s against 198 s for AIOpsLab; GCR 99.9%; removing the deterministic guard left MTTR almost unchanged (144 s) but cut GCR to 72.3%
limitation: No variance reported; baseline implementations not described
title: Autonomous AI Decision Control Tower: A Deterministic Multi-Agent Decision Intelligence Framework for Enterprise NoOps
venue: 2026 IEEE 1st International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Implementation and Applications, ICAIIA 2026

task: Adapting detection and response thresholds in industrial CPS
method: Four hierarchical RL variants (h-DQN, option-critic)
uncertainty: Dynamic instability of the CPS network
act: Select detection and response threshold ranges
constraint: Cost of changing the selected range
env: Simulated industrial CPS with a network data generator
metrics: System damage; false positives; cost
result: All four hierarchical variants outperformed the static threshold method
limitation: Decision is a threshold setting, a borderline case of a triage decision
title: Autonomous and Adaptive Cyber Incident Detection and Response in Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems Using Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
venue: ACM Transactions on Cyber-Physical Systems

task: Ranking root-cause candidates in microservices
method: PPO random walk over a causal graph
uncertainty: Agent observes only its neighbourhood of the causal graph
info: Choose which node of the causal graph to visit next
constraint: Invalid-action masking
env: RCAEval benchmark (eight synthetic and microservice datasets)
baselines: Nine RCA methods from RCAEval and a dummy agent
metrics: AC@k; Avg@5
result: Outperformed the best baselines on five of eight datasets
limitation: Memory and compute demands on large metric sets
title: CauseRL: Reinforcement Learning-based Random Walks for Root Cause Analysis in Microservices
venue: Proceedings of the ACM Symposium on Applied Computing

task: DDoS mitigation in a software-defined network
method: Double DQN
uncertainty: Agent is not told which host is the attacker
act: Raise or lower a host's bandwidth, or do nothing
constraint: Reward on benign packet loss and delay
env: Mininet emulation with generated benign and attack traffic
metrics: Benign packets delivered; delay; bandwidth
robustness: Three attack types and randomised host positions
result: Attacker bandwidth reduced by 96.7%; benign share of delivered packets rose from 29.6% to 85.8% (ICMP) but only to 39.4% under SYN floods
limitation: Small topology; no quantitative baseline
title: DAMS: Double Deep Q-Network Approach for DDoS Attack Mitigation in SDN
venue: ACM International Conference Proceeding Series

task: Cyber incident response for small and medium enterprises
method: One-step lookahead with an uncertainty penalty and post-event parameter learning
uncertainty: Belief over compromise; observation noise (12% false positives, 18% false negatives)
act: Micro-playbooks (isolate host, revoke credentials, restore, preserve evidence)
constraint: Allowable action set restricted by cost and time limits
env: Simulated 50-asset network with a four-phase ransomware scenario
metrics: MTTD, MTTC, MTTR, expected loss, service loss, decision regret
result: MTTR 58.7 min against 95.3 min for the static baseline; expected loss USD 39,500 against 84,000
limitation: Single scenario; the text states both a 38% and a 20-35% MTTR reduction
title: Designing a Scalable and Adaptive Cyber Incident Response (DACIR) Framework for SMEs
venue: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science

task: Early automated intrusion response for IIoT
method: Expert system plus neural fitted Q-iteration
uncertainty: Alerts the rule base cannot classify are passed to RL
act: Void, restrict traffic, restrict credentials, kill processes
constraint: Expert rules decide known threats first; action reputation register; void action to ignore false positives
env: Industrial testbed emulating energy generation
metrics: Time to response; time to recover
result: Mean time to response about 4 min (SSH brute force) and 0.8 min (malware download); recovery took about 7 min when the attacker countered the response
limitation: No baseline; data cannot be shared; intended as a first response before a human expert acts, which is not evaluated
title: Dispatching advanced and adaptive intrusion responses for IIoT-based systems
venue: Future Generation Computer Systems

task: Alert investigation with certified deferral to analysts
method: PPO investigation agent with a dual-threshold conformal deferral layer
uncertainty: Stochastic, class-overlapping evidence; hardened regime with stealthy threats and damped evidence
info: Query logs, investigate lateral movement, query threat intelligence
esc: Escalate to incident response; defer the uncertain band to an analyst
constraint: Statistical error budgets on benign escalation and threat auto-close
env: Simulated SOC with labels drawn from CIC-IDS2017, CSE-CIC-IDS2018 and UNSW-NB15, plus four classifiers on real flows
metrics: Automation share; deferral share; realised error rates against budgets
robustness: Hardened regime; cross-dataset shift (deferral rose to 79-99% for the worst classifiers)
result: Automated 73.7% of decisions at budgets of 0.01 with realised rates 0.0099 and 0.0101, deferring about 26%; language models failed as a second-stage investigator
limitation: Simulator evidence is mechanistic; guarantees need recalibration on labelled data after shift
title: Dual-Threshold Conformal Deferral for Trustworthy Security Alert Triage
venue: Electronics (Switzerland)

task: Choosing which alerts to investigate under an analyst budget
method: Adversarial deep RL in a double-oracle loop
uncertainty: Adaptive attacker who knows the defender policy
info: Select the subset of alerts for analysts to investigate within a budget
constraint: Hard investigation budget per period
env: Suricata alerts on CICIDS2017 and a credit-card fraud dataset
baselines: Heuristic prioritisation baselines from prior work
metrics: Defender loss
result: Outperformed baseline prioritisation policies, including when the adversary adapts
limitation: Assumes known attacker budget and costs
title: Finding needles in a moving haystack: Prioritizing alerts with adversarial reinforcement learning
venue: AAAI 2020 - 34th AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

task: Predictive platform operations and remediation
method: DQN for discrete actions with PPO for resource allocation, plus coordinating agents
uncertainty: Predicted failure probability included in the state
act: Restart, reroute, rollback, scale, failover
constraint: Plans checked against predefined safety constraints (not evaluated)
env: Simulated 500-node hybrid cloud over 90 days
baselines: Rule-based automation; DQN alone; PPO alone
metrics: MTTR; uptime; anomaly precision and recall; manual interventions
result: MTTR 42.6 min to 29.1 min; manual interventions down 47.8%
limitation: No variance; no limitations section
title: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning and Agentic Artificial Intelligence Framework for Predictive Platform Operations and DevOps Orchestration
venue: 7th International Conference on Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing, ICCVBIC 2026 - Proceedings

task: Multi-agent cyber defence with RL and LLM agents
method: KEEP graph PPO agents and LLM agents
uncertainty: Partial observability per network zone
act: Remove, restore, deploy decoy, block or allow zone traffic
constraint: Penalties when legitimate users lose service
env: CybORG CAGE-4
metrics: Reward; running time
result: All-RL team mean reward -493 (sd 95.9) against -2547.2 (sd 498.8) for all-LLM; LLM agents misread communication vectors
limitation: Two episodes per configuration; the reward reflects availability only
title: Large Language Models are Autonomous Cyber Defenders
venue: Proceedings - 2025 IEEE Conference on Artificial Intelligence, CAI 2025

task: Cooperative cyber defence with learned communication
method: DIAL against QMIX
uncertainty: Detection rate 95% or 50%; benign users raise false alerts
info: Analyse (unmasked on detection or a message)
act: Remove, restore, block
constraint: Restore unmasked only for persistent threats; analyse only after a detection or message
env: CybORG with three network configurations
metrics: Mean return with standard deviation
robustness: Detection rate lowered to 50%; false alerts from benign users; larger networks
result: With 50% detection, unmasking and blocking, DIAL agents returned -26.4 against -43.4 for QMIX on the large network
limitation: Communication strategy inconsistent in simple games; no limitations section
title: Learning to Communicate in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Cyber Defence
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Machine Learning and Cybernetics

task: Prioritising Windows Registry analysis during incident response
method: Dynamic programming with bounded tabular RL refinement and rule-based AI
uncertainty: Not represented
info: Choose the next registry or timeline analysis step
constraint: State-dependent action sets; expert policy graphs
env: Four forensic datasets across Windows versions and scenarios
baselines: KAPE and RegRipper pipelines; examiner-led workflows
metrics: Precision; recall; time; time to first relevant artefact
result: Investigation time cut by up to 68% and adjudicated relevant artefacts up by up to 35% against analyst-assisted baselines (10 seeded runs)
limitation: RL is a bounded refinement of a dynamic-programming planner; evidence scope limited to registry and timeline
title: Leveraging reinforcement learning for an efficient windows registry analysis during cyber incident response
venue: Scientific Reports

task: Mission-aware incident response on a military network

uncertainty: Not represented

env: Train Ticket and Online Boutique benchmark data

venue: 7th International Conference on Computational Vision and Bio Inspired Computing, ICCVBIC 2026 - Proceedings

task: Online incident response planning under model misspecification
